findings.description: The inner catch in `mergedOnto` treats every git failure as "no match". A real failure such as git < 2.38, a usage error or exit 128 is reported as "the merge landed content the gate never measured" instead of "Reading what X landed failed".

When the pinned branch holds a merge commit (e.g. a re-gated PR that took main), a GitHub rebase merge flattens it away, so the rebase shape fails and the squash shape matches only the last replayed commit; acceptance stays sound, but the overlap steer's `gitDiffPaths(landedOn, mergeCommit)` misses the earlier replayed commits' files.

`steerOverlappingSessions` gains a seventh positional string parameter, `landedOn`, right next to `mergeCommit`, so the two shas can be swapped without the type checker noticing; passing the pair (or the computed file set) would rule that out.
Three new tests repeat the same seedPrMerge/cloneOrigin/moveOriginMain/squashOnGitHub/fakeGh prelude; a small `squashedOntoMovedMain()` helper beside `squashOnGitHub` would cut each to one line.
`(real as typeof withScratchGitDir)` casts away the possible `undefined` from `getMockImplementation()`, whereas the file's existing version of this pattern (~L385) handles it with `real?.(…)`.

The rebase test's comment says "the last one's tree is checked against the base the first went onto", but `mergedOnto` checks every replayed commit's tree, and ADR 0130 and the JSDoc warn that checking only the last tree is the bug; reword it to say each replayed tree is checked against merging its pinned commit onto the base.
